definition: Producing training or evaluation material with a model rather than collecting it, and across 6 sources the archive's most common way to obtain step-level supervision at scale. The recipes here share a structure: generate with a stronger model, constrain the form, filter by a check, and keep what passes -- grounded chart-reasoning chains with predicted regions, evidence graphs over document blocks, therapy dialogues with an orchestrator steering simulated patients away from sycophantic compliance, typed spatial-reasoning segments. Two cautions the corpus supports. Filtering traces for reaching a known answer selects for post-hoc rationalisations that happen to land correctly, so the corpus is not a sample of anyone's reasoning; several sources report downstream gains from such data anyway, which is the honest finding, but the traces are not accounts of an inference. And where the generator, the filter and the auditor are all models, what the resulting dataset calls a property means what those models judged it to be -- one source states this about its own benchmark, with human involvement confined to adjudicating disagreements.

evidence.note: Reformulates chart question answering as a chain in which every reasoning step carries a predicted image region, trains that pairing through a curriculum graded by nesting depth, and finds explicit intermediate grounding worth 8.78 points over letting the model attend implicitly.
evidence.title: CURV: Enhancing Chart Understanding Through Curriculum Visual Grounded Reasoning

evidence.note: Recasts long-document visual question answering as building an explicit evidence graph whose nodes are grounded document blocks and whose edges are reasoning dependencies, and verifies the graph causally — masking the evidence it cites flips 82.8% of correct answers while masking uncited evidence changes 9.6%.
evidence.title: DocTrace: Towards Traceable Long Document VQA via Hierarchical Evidence Graph Reasoning

evidence.note: Synthesizes Cognitive Behavioral Therapy dialogues using a CoT strategy grounded in CBT guidelines plus a resistance orchestrator that steers simulated patients away from sycophantic compliance.
evidence.title: ODRA: Synthesizing Cognitive Behavioral Therapy Sessions with Structured Chain-Of-Thought and Dynamic Patient Resistance

evidence.note: Splits a spatial-reasoning chain of thought into explicitly typed segments -- perception, including depth, and reasoning -- and gives each its own process reward and its own advantage term, so that the two do not compete for credit under a single outcome signal.
evidence.title: SCOUT: Unlocking Enhanced Spatial Reasoning via Structured Chain-of-Thought and Multi-Objective Process Reward

evidence.note: Benchmarks whether reasoning models follow instructions inside their reasoning traces, finding under 25% compliance at best and worse as difficulty rises.
evidence.title: ReasonIF: Large Reasoning Models Fail to Follow Instructions During Reasoning

evidence.note: A 4B small reasoning model that classifies document-claim pairs as grounded or hallucinated for RAG pipelines and produces evidence-grounded justifications.
evidence.title: HalluGuard: Evidence-Grounded Small Reasoning Models to Mitigate Hallucinations in Retrieval-Augmented Generation

name: synthetic data generation
